PHSCS 587

Self-aligned fabrication

From the figure to the concept

Fig. 1 shows how a gate and its spacers locate source and drain regions

A transistor’s electrical dimensions depend on how successive fabrication patterns line up. In a conceptual self-aligned gate-first process, a patterned gate shields the channel region while exposed regions receive source/drain implantation. The gate edge supplies the alignment reference, reducing the need to align an independent source/drain mask precisely to that edge.

Sidewall spacers establish an additional geometric offset for later processing. Isolation, gate dielectric formation, patterning, doping, activation and contacts all contribute to the resulting cross section. Implant straggle and subsequent thermal diffusion mean that an electrical junction edge is a concentration profile rather than an infinitely sharp mask edge.

Material purity, interface quality and repeatable processing are part of device behavior: they affect traps, mobility, leakage, contact resistance and variability. The diagram conveys the alignment principle. Specific modern technologies can use different gate ordering, replacement-gate steps and three-dimensional geometries, so a complete process flow must match the intended technology.

Example

A wider sidewall spacer can increase the offset of a later source/drain implant from the gate edge. The final electrical overlap still depends on implantation and thermal evolution, so spacer width alone does not fix every junction dimension.
